short: Building software by describing what you want in plain language and letting a model write the code.
why: It moves the hard part from typing to specifying and checking. If you can't tell whether what came back is right, speed just gets you to the wrong place sooner.
hear_it: "I vibe-coded the whole thing in an afternoon."

short: Large language model — the thing doing the writing. It predicts what text should come next, very well, over and over.
why: Knowing it predicts rather than looks up explains almost every surprising thing it does, including the confident wrong answers.

short: A specific trained version you can talk to, with a name and a price — Opus, Sonnet, Haiku.
why: They differ in cost, speed and how much reasoning they'll do. Reaching for the biggest one every time is a way to spend money on nothing.
hear_it: "Switch to a smaller model for this one."

short: What you actually asked for — the text you send.
why: Almost every bad result is a prompt that left something unsaid. Vague in, vague out, and the model will not tell you what it guessed.

short: The unit a model reads and writes in — roughly three quarters of a word.
why: Everything you pay for and every limit you hit is counted in these, not in words or lines. It's the meter on the taxi.

short: Everything the model can see at once — your prompt, the files it read, the whole conversation so far.
why: When it fills up, earlier things fall out of view. Most "it forgot what I said" moments are this, not the model being stupid.

short: Standing instructions the model carries into every message, set before you start typing.
why: It is why the same question gets different answers in two different tools. When behaviour seems inexplicable, this is usually where the explanation lives.
hear_it: "That must be coming from the system prompt."

short: A confident, fluent, completely made-up answer — a function that doesn't exist, a citation nobody wrote.
why: It arrives in exactly the same tone as a correct answer. There is no tell, which is the entire reason you verify instead of trusting.

short: A model that can take actions — read files, run commands, search — not just produce text.
why: The moment it can act, mistakes stop being wrong paragraphs and start being deleted files. This is where permissions begin to matter.

short: Act, look at the result, decide what to do next, repeat — until the job is done or it gives up.
why: It explains why an agent can fix its own mistakes, and why it can also spend twenty minutes confidently going in a circle.

short: The same question can get a different answer twice.
why: It means "it worked when I tried it" is weak evidence, and a bug that vanishes on retry has not been fixed.
hear_it: "It worked the first time, I swear."
